about: The `delayexpr` of a <send> is a string computed from the machine's fields when the send runs, and read as the CSS2 time it must be: `wait + 'ms'` over a uint32 holding 100 is 100ms. A step with `advance_ms` moves the machine's time on by that many milliseconds before the machine is read; the margins are wide (nothing is due within a few milliseconds of a step's end) so an engine on a real clock reads the same answer as one on a manual clock. `slow` doubles the wait of the NEXT send, the one armed already keeps the wait it was armed with. `soon` is no CSS2 time and `huge` overflows the uint32, each raises error.execution and the message is not sent at all. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: armed: due in 100ms, not delivered yet
100ms later it has been delivered, once
the wait changes; nothing is armed
the next send is armed with the wait it holds now: 200ms
100ms later it is not due: the wait was read when the send ran
another 200ms later it has been delivered
a string that is no CSS2 time: an argument that cannot be evaluated
and the message is never delivered, however long it waits
a delay that does not fit its type fails as any other operation does
and that message is not delivered either
